_comment: THE CAPTURE CONTRACT. This is the single source of truth for what a working
capture looks like on an Alibaba suppliers results page. Two checkers read it:
tools/contract-check.mjs  verifies the live page still has these anchors and
that a real capture fills these fields
test/contract.test.js    is the same contract as a unit test
A failure here means Alibaba changed the page, NOT that the user did something
wrong. Fix the extractor against the page, never against a guess.
Rules that exist because guessing caused three broken releases:
- anchors must be data-* attributes, alt text or labels, never class names
- every required field must be present on at least this share of rows
- 'minRows' is the floor for a real results page; below it the page is
still loading or the user must scroll

anchors.means: product URL, used for the title slug

forbiddenAnchors.why: Alibaba hashes class names per deploy; they change without warning

fields.from: span[title] that is not inside a product tile
img[alt=countryFlag], code in the next sibling
the first price line of each product tile
the symbol on that price line, US$ means USD
'Min. order: N unit' inside the same product tile
the '4.8/5' text next to the name
the text before the country flag

honesty.comment: Rules the UI must keep, checked by tools/panel-preview.mjs.
honesty.noSilentHiding: If any row is hidden by a filter, the panel names the filter, says how many rows, and offers one click to clear them.
honesty.noInventedValues: A field the page does not publish shows '—' or 'not shown'. It is never guessed.
honesty.rangeIsHonest: A published range keeps both ends; the low end ranks and the high end is shown and exported.
honesty.degradedIsLoud: A capture missing a required field on more than a fifth of its rows raises a banner naming the field.
